1. Given f(x) = x³ − 3x, find its maximum and minimum on [−2, 2].
Solution: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 3(x + 1)(x − 1). Setting f′(x) = 0 gives x = −1 or x = 1. Comparing endpoints and stationary points gives a maximum of 2 and minimum of −2.
2. The line y = kx + 1 meets the parabola y = x² at A and B. Find the length of AB.
3. Given a₁ = 1 and aₙ₊₁ = 2aₙ + 1, find the general term of {aₙ} and justify your answer.
